title: Transplanting Seedlings onto a Permanent Bed
summary: The 6 steps to lift, trim and transplant your nursery-grown seedlings onto a permanent bed without root stress.

pages.title: Transplanting seedlings onto a permanent bed
pages.illustration_description: Une agricultrice ouest-africaine accroupie dans le passe-pied en terre, transplantant soigneusement de jeunes plants de tomates avec leurs mottes sur une planche permanente en pleine terre quadrillée.

pages.title: Which crops should be transplanted?
pages.text:
Transplanting applies to a wide variety of vegetables that need good root development before final planting out:

- **Grown in an in-ground nursery**: lettuces, celery, onions, cabbages.
- **Already pricked out into pots**: tomatoes, sweet peppers, hot peppers, eggplants.

Make sure your beds are already **loosened, leveled, moistened and labeled** before you begin.
pages.illustration_description: Composition botanique en aquarelle montrant de jeunes plants vigoureux prêts à être transplantés : un plant de tomate en petit pot, un plant de chou et un plant d'oignon avec leurs racines saines.

pages.title: Materials and tools needed
pages.text:
Gather the following equipment before starting:

- Your nursery-grown **seedlings**
- 1 knife or 1 transplanting trowel
- 1 small hoe (to dig holes if needed)
- 1 measuring tape, 1 spacing marker and 1 string line
- 1 fine-toothed rake
- 1 watering can (if there is no sprinkler irrigation)
- Straw
- *Optional*: 1 shade net
pages.illustration_description: Outils de transplantation disposés en aquarelle sur la terre chaude : transplantoir, petite houe, couteau de jardin, corde, traceur de distance, arrosoir et caissette de jeunes plants verts.

pages.title: Step 1: Lifting seedlings from an in-ground nursery (1/2)
pages.text:
1. **Water the seedlings thoroughly** in the nursery before lifting them.
2. Use a knife or a transplanting trowel to cut the soil around the seedlings: make a clean, deep cut **3–4 cm** from the plant to detach the roots without damaging them.
3. Gently lift the root ball, keeping as **much soil as possible** around the roots.
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan en aquarelle sur des mains ouest-africaines découpant délicatement une motte de terre humide autour d'un jeune plant avec un transplantoir afin de préserver tout le système racinaire.

pages.title: Step 1: Protecting the roots and puddling (2/2)
pages.text:
4. If you are not transplanting right away, put the root ball back in its original spot to prevent the roots from drying out, and water lightly.
5. If the soil does not hold together around the roots, **dip the roots in a well-mixed slurry of soil and water** (puddling): this mud sticks to the roots and promotes excellent establishment.
pages.illustration_description: Mains ouest-africaines trempant délicatement les racines nues d'un jeune plant dans une bassine contenant une bouillie fluide de terre et d'eau avant la plantation.

pages.title: Step 2: Preparing potted seedlings
pages.text:
For seedlings already grown in pots (tomatoes, sweet peppers, hot peppers, eggplants):

- **Water them thoroughly** before transplanting so that the root ball stays cohesive.
- **Remove the plant from its pot only at the last moment**, just before planting it, to prevent the roots from drying out.
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan en aquarelle sur des mains ouest-africaines démoulant délicatement un jeune plant de tomate bien humide hors de son pot recyclé, révélant une motte intacte entourée de racines blanches.

pages.title: Step 3: Trimming seedlings before transplanting
pages.text:
Proper preparation of the seedling limits water loss through evapotranspiration, focuses its energy on root recovery and reduces the risk of disease.

**Techniques by crop:**
- **Onions**: cut about **1/3 of the foliage**.
- **Lettuces**: remove the large outer leaves and keep the heart.
- **Beets**: remove 2 to 3 large leaves and leave the young ones intact.
- **Tomatoes, sweet peppers, hot peppers**: remove the first flowers (to avoid fruiting too early) as well as any yellowed or damaged leaves.
pages.illustration_description: Planche pédagogique en aquarelle montrant trois gestes d'habillage par des mains ouest-africaines : couper le haut du feuillage d'un jeune oignon, retirer une grande feuille externe d'une laitue, et pincer la première fleur d'un jeune plant de tomate.

pages.title: Step 4: Marking out the grid on the bed
pages.text:
1. Determine the **number of rows** and the **spacing between rows** (examples: 1 row, 2 rows spaced 60 cm apart, 3 rows spaced 25 cm apart, 4 rows spaced 20 cm apart) according to the crop data sheet.
2. Mark out **perfectly parallel** rows with a marker or a stick.
3. Then mark **perpendicular** lines corresponding to the in-row plant spacing.
4. The **grid intersections** show the exact position of each seedling.
pages.illustration_description: Un agriculteur ouest-africain traçant un quadrillage régulier à la surface d'une planche permanente en pleine terre nivelée à l'aide d'un traceur, créant des repères nets pour la plantation.

pages.title: Step 5: Installing a string trellis support (staking)
pages.text:
Some climbing or tall crops (tomatoes, cucumbers) need a **string support** to grow well, reduce disease, keep them from trailing on the ground and make the best use of space.

**Installation:**
1. Before setting the plant, insert the end of the string at the bottom of the planting hole to anchor it firmly.
2. Securely tie the other end to the support structure (**trellis**), keeping the string taut but flexible.
3. As the plant grows, gradually tie in the main stem.
pages.illustration_description: Planche permanente en pleine terre surmontée d'un treillis simple en piquets locaux avec des ficelles descendant verticalement jusqu'aux trous de plantation, un maraîcher ouest-africain fixant une ficelle.

pages.title: Step 6: Setting the plants at the intersections (1/2)
pages.text:
1. Bring the seedlings from the nursery, handling them with care, and place them at the grid intersections.
2. Dig a hole that is **slightly wider and deeper than the root ball** to make it easier for the roots to settle in.
pages.illustration_description: Vue rapprochée en aquarelle d'une planche de pleine terre quadrillée où une agricultrice ouest-africaine creuse un trou adapté à la taille de la motte à l'aide d'une petite houe ou d'un transplantoir.

pages.title: Step 6: Planting and firming without air pockets (2/2)
pages.text:
3. Place the seedling at the bottom of the hole, making sure the **roots are in direct contact with the soil**, with no empty space or air pockets.
4. Put the soil back around the roots and **press lightly** with your fingers to stabilize the plant and keep it upright.
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan en aquarelle sur deux mains ouest-africaines ramenant la terre fertile autour d'un jeune plant installé bien droit dans son trou et tassant doucement autour du collet.

pages.title: What comes next? Care right after planting
pages.text:
After transplanting, some essential tasks remain: the **initial watering**, a **thin layer of mulch**, possibly installing an **insect net**, followed by hoeing, hilling and weeding (see module **M3.4.4**).

**Congratulations**, you have just transplanted your seedlings onto your permanent growing bed!
pages.illustration_description: Planche permanente en pleine terre fraîchement transplantée avec des rangées régulières de jeunes plants bien droits, entourés d'un léger paillage et de passe-pieds propres, sous une lumière douce.
